query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a thin, oxide-forming element coating, such as aluminum or silicon, to the surface of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.intervention: Application of a thin, oxide-forming element coating
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at temperatures up to 1000 °C for times up to several hours, with strain rates of 10⁻⁴-10⁻² s⁻¹
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer on the surface
generation.mechanism: The oxide layer prevents oxygen from penetrating to the underlying alloy, reducing oxidation and improving resistance to high-temperature degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, reduced oxidation, and enhanced high-temperature mechanical performance
generation.boundary: Temperature: up to 1000 °C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: several hours, Loading: strain rates of 10⁻⁴-10⁻² s⁻¹
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the coating in improving oxygen resistance and the optimal coating composition and thickness are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation resistance of coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples exposed to air at 800 °C for 5 hours
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated sample shows no significant improvement in oxidation resistance or mechanical properties compared to the uncoated sample, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How can high-entropy alloys be designed to achieve simultaneous high damping capacity, high strength, and high ductility at elevated temperatures via Snoek relaxation?. System: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA). Test conditions: Damping: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 Hz, 300 to 1100 K, heating rate 2 K min−1, strain amplitude 2 × 10−4; Mechanical: Room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1. Question: What are the individual effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on the microstructure and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and elevated-temperature performance) of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys?. System: Equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr and its five sub-alloys created by the subtraction method: HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting of 99.9 wt.% (99.99 wt.% for Ti) pure elements stacked by melting point, re-melted at least four times, and solidified in a water-cool copper mold. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C, and 1400 °C; crosshead speed 0.36 mm/min (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); cylindrical samples 3.6 mm diameter x 6 mm height.
